key_insight: CG-OMatG uses an equivariant Riemannian flow model with reinforcement learning to generate molecular crystal structures by learning coarse-grained packing, orientations, and lattice parameters.
engineering_relevance: This could speed up polymorph screening and organic materials discovery by proposing low-energy crystal candidates more efficiently than brute-force search.
method: Treats each molecule as a rigid body and uses hierarchical inter- and intra-molecular message passing.
Learns to reconstruct centroid positions, orientations, and lattice parameters conditioned on chemical species and conformer geometry.
Fine-tunes generation with policy-gradient reinforcement learning to favor low-energy structures.
evidence_signal: The model is trained on subsets of OMC25 and CSD and validated on the CSP blind test benchmark using COMPACK packing-similarity analysis against experimentally determined crystals.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of training crystal datasets, and rigid-body coarse-graining may miss important flexible-molecule effects.
paper_title: Riemannian Flow Models with Reinforcement Learning for Molecular Crystal Structure Prediction
